The maximum fine for failing to provide a copy of an assignment of rights to the Registered Agent or Registrar within 30 days is $1,500, as specified in Schedule 3, Article 10(7) of the Foundations Law DIFC Law No. 3 of 2018.

The Board of Directors of the DIFCA is responsible for appointing and dismissing the Registrar. They must consult the President prior to making such appointments or dismissals, as stated in Article 2(2) and (3) of the Operating Law - DIFC Law No. 7 of 2018.

DIFC Law No. 2 of 2022 amended the following specific DIFC Laws: 
1. Employment Law (DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019)
2. Law on the Application of Civil and Commercial Laws in the DIFC (DIFC Law No. 3 of 2004)
3. Foundations Law (DIFC Law No. 3 of 2018)
4. Common Reporting Standard Law (DIFC Law No. 2 of 2018)
ONORA

The application in case SCT 169/2025 was dismissed. The Judgment upheld claims made by the Claimant, Oleta, against the Defendant Applicant, Onesimo, for payment of her September salary of AED 3,466.67 and Court fees of AED 367.25, rejecting the Applicant's defense of set-off.

The effective date for due diligence requirements under the Common Reporting Standard Law 2018 is 31 December 2016 for Pre-existing Accounts and 1 January 2017 for New Accounts as specified in Section 6 of the Law.
The Personal Property Law 2005 was made by the Ruler of Dubai, as stated in Article 2 of the Law.

Article 16(1)(c) of the Employment Law 2019 requires an Employer to retain records of an Employee's remuneration during the Employee's employment and for six (6) years after the Employee's Termination Date. These records must include various deductions, leave taken, and payments made to the Employee.

The outcome of the No Costs Application in case CFI 016/2025 was that it was dismissed, with no order as to costs for this application. The Claimant was ordered to pay AED 70,000 in costs to the Defendant as per the Judgment dated 19 September 2025.

According to Article 12(4) of the Common Reporting Standard Law, records must be retained for a period of six (6) years after the date of reporting the information. There is no specified retention period mentioned in Article 18(2)(b) of the General Partnership Law in the provided context.

The application in case CFI 067/2025, submitted by the Defendant seeking immediate judgment or to strike out, was dismissed by H.E. Justice Shamlan Al Sawalehi on 26 January 2026. The Applicant was ordered to pay 80% of the Respondent’s costs, totaling USD 155,879.50.

A Reporting Financial Institution that obtains or creates records in a language other than English must, upon request, provide an English translation of those records to the Relevant Authority as per Article 12(5) of the Common Reporting Standard Law 2018.

The administration of the Employment Law and any Regulations made under it is the responsibility of the DIFCA (Dubai International Financial Centre Authority) as stated in Article 8.

The administration of the Foundation, as per the Foundations Law, is governed by the officers of the Foundation. Their powers, obligations, liabilities, and rights, as well as their appointment and removal, are subject to the laws of the DIFC (Article 5(1)(c)).

The purpose of Article 9(1) of the Foundations Law is to mandate that a Foundation must have a Charter that is in the English language. This ensures clarity and uniformity in the foundational document, facilitating understanding and compliance with the law.
